chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Saif from Mansur who said: A trustworthy companion of ours narrated to me who said:

I was walking in some of the streets of Mecca when a man met me and said to me, 'Slaughter these two birds for me.' So I slaughtered them, forgetting, while I was in the state of Ihram (Halal). Then I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said, 'Upon you is the price (compensation).'

key_terms.حَلَالٌ: in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering a bird while in Ihram if done out of forgetfulness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* illustrates the principle of *al-gharam* (financial compensation) for unintentional violations of Ihram restrictions, specifically the hunting of game. It highlights the scholarly distinction between forgetting one's state (*nasi*) and deliberate action, establishing that the pilgrim remains liable for the value of the slaughtered birds despite the lack of intent.
